# Loop 0 — Bootstrap

**Goal:** confirm you can actually do the work before you promise any of it.

**Output:** a capability line in `runs/<slug>/REPORT.md`. Nothing else.

---

## The capabilities

| # | Capability | Native check | If missing |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Shell + git** | `git --version` | Stop. Nothing works without it |
| 2 | **Web fetch / search** | your own tools | Loop 1 competitor teardown and VOC mining are unavailable. Record the skip |
| 3 | **Headless browser** | `browse` skill, or Playwright | Loops 2b, 4, 7 lose screenshots and Loop 7 loses the funnel proof. **This is the one to fix** — `§18` needs a real browser |
| 4 | **Crawler** | `npx lychee`, or `wget --spider`, or the browser | Loop 1's redirect map is built from the sitemap alone, which misses orphan pages (`§13`) |
| 5 | **Image generation** | `imagegen-frontend-web` or equivalent | Loop 2a runs as written concepts instead of images; Gate B1 gets worse |
| 6 | **Image sampling** | `python3 -c "import PIL"` | `pip install Pillow`, or ImageMagick, or the brand palette gets guessed (`§12`) |
| 7 | **Prose skills** | `stop-slop`, `copywriting`, `ogilvy` | Install via `find-skills`. Loop 3 degrades without them |
| 8 | **Audit tooling** | `npx @axe-core/cli`, `npx lighthouse` | Loop 7 checks become manual. `§17` still applies |
| 9 | **GitHub API** | `gh auth status` | Only needed if the client's repo or Pages is the target |
| 10 | **Deploy CLI** | depends on target — see below | Loop 6 becomes handoff mode |

Check them, report what you have in one line, and move on. Do not spend a long time
here.

## Client-side access — ask, don't check

Four things you cannot verify yourself and should ask for now, so they exist by the
time they are needed. They are the most common reason a run stalls in the middle.

| Access | Needed by | Ask for |
|---|---|---|
| Analytics | Loop 1 baseline, Loop 5, Loop 8 | Read access on their property, on their account |
| Search Console | Loop 1 redirect map, Loop 7, Loop 8 | Verified property access — the authoritative ranking list |
| CRM / lead destination | Loop 5, Loop 7 (`§18`) | Where leads go, who reads them, and a way to confirm arrival |
| DNS and host | Loop 6 | Whose account, who can change records, current TTL |

## The deploy CLI

Cannot be checked until the target is known, which happens in Loop 1. Re-run this row
after Gate A.

| Target | Check |
|---|---|
| GitHub Pages | `gh auth status` |
| Netlify | `netlify --version` |
| Vercel | `vercel --version` |
| Cloudflare Pages | `wrangler --version` |
| VPS (nginx or Docker) | `ssh <host> 'echo ok'`, then `docker --version` on the host if relevant |
| cPanel | `lftp --version`, or `curl --version` with FTPS |
| S3 + CloudFront | `aws sts get-caller-identity` |
| Handoff | nothing |

A missing CLI is not a blocker. Say which one, offer to install it, and continue — the
target only has to work by Loop 6.

## Set up the run

```bash
mkdir -p runs/<slug>/{shots,prototypes,inbox,design,baseline}
cp runs/_template/*.md runs/<slug>/
```

`<slug>` is the client's domain or name, lowercased and hyphenated. `inbox/` is where
they drop material for Loop 1 — brand book, sales deck, customer quotes, support
exports, the claims they want to make. Tell them it exists now, so the material is
there by the time you need it.

`baseline/` is where Loop 1's analytics exports and screenshots go. It is small,
boring, and the only reason Loop 8 can say anything honest.

## Existing site or not

One question, asked here rather than in Loop 1, because the answer changes what Loop 1
has to do first.

| Answer | Loop 1 must also |
|---|---|
| Replacing a site on the same domain | Crawl it, export the ranking URLs, build the redirect map (`§13`, hard). Capture the baseline before anything changes |
| New domain, nothing to replace | One sentence: "nothing to preserve." Move on |
| New site, old one stays somewhere | Decide what happens to the old URLs. "Both live" is usually two sites competing for the same terms |

## What not to do here

Do not research the client. Do not propose a design. Do not ask the intake questions —
those belong to Loop 1 and they work better opening the conversation than following a
capability audit.

## Skip cost

Skipping bootstrap costs you a failure in Loop 6 or 7 instead of a two-minute check in
Loop 0, plus the client-access requests arriving three loops late. It is the cheapest
loop to run and the most annoying one to have skipped.

---
name: site-verifier
description: Loop 7 worker for webcrab. Runs the 24-check live checklist against the LIVE URL, never the local build. Screenshots every template at 360/768/1440 in both color modes and reduced motion, runs axe and Lighthouse, checks Core Web Vitals against the budget, verifies the robots/sitemap/canonical plumbing, and verifies the redirect map including all top-20-by-traffic rows. Writes REPORT.md with an honest confidence grade graded against SKIPS.md, failures on the first page. Returns the grade, the failures, and the report path.
tools: Bash, Read, Write, Grep
---

You are the verification worker for the webcrab pipeline. You confirm with your eyes
that the live site renders, that it can be found, and that it is not breaking what the
client already had. `funnel-verifier` covers the conversion path in parallel.

**Verify the live URL, never the local build.** Local and live differ in ways that
matter: absolute paths, MIME types, compression, cache headers, TLS, redirects, and
whatever the host rewrites. `HTTP 200` is not "it renders" (`§14` of the verify loop).

## The 24 checks

Follow `loops/07-verify.md`. Run all of them, on every template, and record what you
observed rather than what you expected.

**Renders** — 1 at 360/768/1440 · 2 both color modes · 3 reduced motion · 4 no-WebGL
and no-JS fallback · 5 at 320px and 200% zoom

**Accessible** — 6 keyboard, focus, traps, skip link, focus return · 7 axe with **zero
violations, not zero criticals** · 8 contrast measured on the live render including
over imagery and after any grade · 9 alt text on every image · 10 form labels, error
association, no color-only signaling

**Fast** — 11 Lighthouse mobile, all four scores · 12 LCP, INP, CLS against the Gate B2
budget on a throttled profile · 13 shell under 100KB and heavy layer deferred · 14 no
layout shift after paint, cookie banner included · 15 console clean on load and after a
full scroll

**Found** — 16 `robots.txt` and no production `noindex`, checked on the **live output**
· 17 sitemap of live canonical URLs, referenced from robots · 18 one hostname, one
protocol, one trailing-slash rule, single hop · 19 redirects: **all** top-20-by-traffic
rows plus a sample of the rest · 20 titles, descriptions, one `h1`, heading order,
canonicals absolute and self-referential · 21 structured data validates and matches
visible content

**Converts** — 22 the funnel (owned by `funnel-verifier`; carry its result into the
report) · 23 unfurl · 24 every link clicked, zero 404s

## Starting points

```bash
mkdir -p runs/<slug>/shots/live
for w in 360 768 1440; do
  chrome --headless --window-size=$w,1400 --screenshot=runs/<slug>/shots/live/$w.png "<live-url>"
done
npx @axe-core/cli "<live-url>"
npx lighthouse "<live-url>" --output=json --output-path=runs/<slug>/lh-mobile.json --quiet
npx lychee --no-progress "<live-url>"
curl -sI "https://<domain>" | head -20
curl -s "https://<domain>/robots.txt"
curl -s "https://<domain>/sitemap.xml" | head -40

# the redirect map — every row, status and destination
while IFS=, read -r old new status _; do
  printf '%s -> %s\n' "$old" "$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' "https://<domain>$old")"
done < <(tail -n +2 runs/<slug>/redirects.csv)
```

## Two findings that stop everything

Report these first, above the grade, and tell the conductor they need fixing before
anything else:

- **A production `noindex` or `Disallow: /`.** The site is invisible and nobody will
  notice for weeks. This is the most common catastrophic launch bug and it is silent
- **A redirect map row returning 404 or 200-at-the-old-URL.** Either the map was not
  applied or the old page is still live and competing. `§13` is hard

## Handle failures

Fix what is fixable now, re-verify, and record **both** states. Log the rest with what
it would take to fix.

- **Never report a fix you did not confirm**
- Never paper over a failure with a caveat. If check 7 found axe violations, that goes
  on the first page of the report, never in a footnote
- Never grade around a failure. The grade reflects what is true

## Write `runs/<slug>/REPORT.md`

It opens with the confidence grade and its reason, then the failures, then everything
else.

| Grade | Means |
|---|---|
| **A** | Full pipeline. Claims substantiated, positioning derived from real market and customer evidence, design validated at both gates, funnel proven live, instrumented and measurable |
| **B** | Core intact, some validation skipped. Strategy or design review thinner than ideal. Everything hard still held |
| **C** | Substance skipped — no VOC, no competitor work, or no real copy pass. A good-looking site making the client's own claims in the client's own words |
| **D** | Multiple substance skips, or shipped without measurement. A redesign whose effect nobody will ever know. Say exactly that |

Read `runs/<slug>/SKIPS.md` and grade against it. A **D** stated plainly is more useful
than an **A** claimed falsely; the grade exists so the client knows what they have.

Then: the live URL and target, all 24 checks with results, the screenshot paths, the
Lighthouse and CWV numbers against the budget, the redirect verification with the
top-20 called out, `funnel-verifier`'s result including its two partial steps, what was
skipped and what it cost, the rollback command, every claim the conductor flagged and
the client overruled, and what would move the grade up.

## What you return

The grade with its reason, the failures in full, the two stop-everything checks
explicitly, and the path to `REPORT.md`.

You are labor, not a decision-maker. The conductor looks at your screenshots afterward,
because an automated pass and a page that looks wrong are compatible states. You cannot
talk to the client. Never push to a remote and never deploy.

# Loop 4 — Build

**Goal:** the site exists, coded to the approved images, with real copy in it, in all
three states, under budget, and editable by the client.

**Input:** `DIRECTION.md`, the design images, `COPY.md`, the prototypes.

**Output:** the site, in the client's repository.

---

## Stack

Settled at Gate A (`ARCHITECTURE.md`). Default is hand-authored HTML and CSS with
committed assets — it runs on all nine deploy targets and it is the fastest thing that
can be built. A publishing cadence moves it to a generator; a non-technical editor
moves it to a CMS.

**Do not ship a framework to the browser for a marketing site.** It is the most common
reason a company site fails Core Web Vitals, and Core Web Vitals are a ranking input
(`§19`). A generator that outputs static HTML is a build-time tool and is fine.

## The shell contract, first

Before any page is built, one person builds the shell and everything else consumes it.
Parallel page builds that each invent their own spacing scale produce a site that
looks assembled, which is exactly what this pipeline exists to avoid.

The shell owns:

### The token file

One file. Every value in it, nothing hardcoded anywhere else.

- Color: substrate, surfaces, text ramp, accent, and the full state set — error,
  success, warning, focus, disabled. Both modes, art-directed separately
- Type: families, the scale, line heights, measures, and the separate mobile scale
- Space: one scale, used everywhere
- Radius, border, shadow: the small set the design actually uses
- Motion: durations and easings from the motion spec, and the reduced-motion values
- Breakpoints and container widths
- Z-index: a named ladder, so the sticky CTA and the cookie banner and the nav do not
  fight in production

### The head

Charset, viewport, title and description per page, canonical, OG and Twitter tags,
favicon set, theme-color, preloads for the LCP image and any font in the LCP element,
and the JSON-LD block. Loop 5 fills the per-page values; the shape lives here.

### The frame

Skip link, header, nav, footer, and the `§27` attribution. Keyboard reachable, current
page indicated, works at 360px, and present on every page including the deepest post.

### The primitives

Buttons, links, form fields, labels, help text, error and success states, tables,
cards, and the section wrapper. Every one with hover, focus-visible, active, and
disabled states designed rather than defaulted.

Build the form primitives properly here, once. They are the `§18` surface and every
page reuses them.

## Fan out

Dispatch `page-builder`, one agent per page, each in its own git worktree so parallel
builds do not collide. Each agent codes **its page only** — never the shell, never the
tokens, never another page's section.

Give each one: its design image, its copy from `COPY.md`, the shell contract, the
technique assignment from `DIRECTION.md`, and the prototype for that technique.

When an agent finds a spec ambiguity, it reports rather than deciding. A builder
inventing a spacing value is how a design system quietly gets a second one.

## Code to the image

The approved design image is the spec. Match the composition, the type scale, the
spacing rhythm, the crop, and the color. Where the image and the copy disagree —
because real copy is longer than the render assumed — the copy wins and the layout
adapts. Note it, so the pattern shows up if it repeats.

Do not redesign during the build. If the image is wrong, that goes back to the
conductor, not into the code.

## Responsive

Three widths minimum, real designs at each: 360, 768, 1440. Not one design that
shrinks.

- **Mobile first, actually.** Most B2B traffic is now mobile, including the buying
  committee's first look, and the champion frequently forwards a link that gets opened
  on a phone
- Fluid type with clamps, and a separate mobile type scale where the display sizes
  need one
- Container queries for components living in more than one context
- Test at 320px and at 200% zoom — both are `§17` requirements and both break
  display-scale typography
- Tables get a real mobile design, not a horizontal scroll of the desktop table
- The primary CTA is reachable on mobile without hunting. A sticky ask is allowed if
  it does not cover the content that argues for it

## Images and media

- Modern formats with fallbacks, `srcset` and `sizes` real rather than decorative
- Explicit `width` and `height` on everything, always. Layout shift after paint is a
  Core Web Vitals failure and the cheapest one to avoid
- LCP image preloaded, correctly sized, never lazy-loaded
- Everything below the fold lazy
- Descriptive `alt` on every image (`§17`), meaningful filenames (`SEO.md`)
- Video: poster image in the shell, player loaded on interaction, never autoplay with
  sound, captions on anything with speech
- Product screenshots at the resolution that makes the UI legible — a blurred
  dashboard is worse than no dashboard (`§11`)

## The three states, per section

Every technique, every time (`§17`):

| State | What ships |
|---|---|
| **Full** | The designed experience |
| **Reduced motion** | An art-directed still. A composed frame someone designed, never `animation: none` |
| **Fallback** | No WebGL, no JS, blocked scripts, old GPU. A real page, never an apology |

The fallback matters commercially here: the visitor on locked-down corporate hardware
is frequently the enterprise buyer.

## Forms

Built here, wired in Loop 5. Per `CONVERSION.md §4`:

- Semantic markup, visible associated labels, correct `type` and `autocomplete`
- Validate on blur, errors next to the field in words, announced to assistive tech
- **Never clear the form on error.** Never lose what they typed
- Submit disabled only while in flight, with a changed label
- Real success state on the page, saying what happens next and when
- Failure state with a route out — an email address to write to instead
- Honeypot and a time-to-submit threshold (`CONVERSION.md §4`)
- It works with JavaScript disabled, or it degrades to a `mailto:` that at least tells
  the visitor the truth

## Vendor everything (`§14`)

Before the build is done: every library, font, and icon downloaded, committed, and
served from the client's own origin. No CDN in production. Pin versions. Keep the
licenses in the repo (`COMPLIANCE.md §3`).

Prototypes were allowed to pull from anywhere. That freedom ends here.

## Third-party tags

Only the ones approved at Gate B2, each loaded after consent (`§16`) and after first
paint (`§15`). None of them in the LCP path. Reserve space for anything that injects
into the layout, including the cookie banner — a banner that shifts the page after
paint is a CLS failure the compliance team mandated and nobody measured.

Whatever was decided at Gate A (`ARCHITECTURE.md`), build it now rather than
retrofitting:

- Content collections with typed frontmatter, if a generator
- CMS schema with typed fields — heading, body, image with **required** alt text — and
  no way to set a color or a font size
- Preview before publish, drafts that do not leak into RSS or the sitemap
- A build that cannot deploy a broken page

| Pass | Check |
|---|---|

| **axe** | Zero violations, not zero criticals |
| **Contrast** | Measured on the rendered pixels, including over imagery and translucency |
| **Copy** | Every string from `COPY.md`, none invented during the build, no lorem left |
| **Claims** | Nothing on the page that is not in `EVIDENCE.md` (`§6`) |
| **Budget** | Shell under 100KB, heavy layer deferred, third-party within its number |
| **Console** | Zero errors on load and after a full scroll |
| **Links** | Every internal link resolves. No dead anchors |
| **Print** | The pricing page prints. Procurement prints pricing pages |
| **No-JS** | The page renders and the content is readable |

## Local screenshots

Screenshot every template at 360, 768, and 1440, in both color modes and with reduced
motion forced, into `runs/<slug>/shots/local/`. Look at them yourself. This is a
rehearsal for Loop 7, and it is much cheaper to fix here.

## Attribution (`§27`)

Small footer credit, "Built with webcrab", linking to the repo and to PIIIX, plus the
marker comment. Visible, never hidden. Tell the client it is there and that removing
it is fine.

## Skip cost

Skipping the quality passes moves cross-browser and responsive failures from before
deploy to after it, where the client finds them.

Skipping the vendoring step leaves the site depending on public endpoints that will
eventually go down and leave it broken, on a domain the client's customers visit.

is a rebuild of the templates.

# Loop 7 — Verify

**Goal:** confirm with your eyes and with a real submission that the live site renders,
ranks, and converts. Then write down honestly what this run produced.

**Input:** the live URL, `FUNNEL.md`, `redirects.csv`, `SKIPS.md`.

**Output:** `runs/<slug>/REPORT.md` with a confidence grade, and `shots/live/`.

---

## Verify the live URL, never the local build

Local and live differ in ways that matter: absolute paths, MIME types, compression,
cache headers, TLS, redirects, and whatever the host rewrites. `HTTP 200` is not "it
renders", and a form that worked locally can post to nowhere in production.

Two agents run in parallel: `site-verifier` for the checklist, `funnel-verifier` for
the conversion path. The conductor looks at the screenshots afterward, because an
automated pass and a page that looks wrong are compatible states.

## The checklist — 24 checks

### Renders

1. **360 / 768 / 1440**, every template. Nothing overflows, collapses, or overlaps.
   Screenshot each into `shots/live/`
2. **Both color modes.** Both designed. Neither an inversion artifact
3. **Reduced motion.** Forced on, still a designed page
4. **Fallback.** Block WebGL and block JS. The page still carries its content
5. **320px and 200% zoom.** Both `§17` requirements, both break display type

### Accessible (`§17`, hard)

6. **Keyboard.** Tab everything, including the form and any modal. Visible focus, no
   traps, skip link works, focus returns after a dialog closes
7. **axe.** Zero violations, not zero criticals
8. **Contrast.** Body text at 4.5:1 measured on the live render, including over
   imagery, translucency, and after any grade or grain
9. **Alt text.** Every image, descriptive, never a filename
10. **Forms.** Labels associated, errors announced and linked to their field, no
    color-only signaling

### Fast (`§19`)

11. **Lighthouse mobile.** Record all four scores
12. **Core Web Vitals** on a throttled mid-range profile: LCP, INP, CLS against the
    Gate B2 budget
13. **Shell budget.** Under 100KB, heavy layer deferred and out of the LCP path
14. **No layout shift after paint**, cookie banner included
15. **Console.** Zero errors on load and after a full scroll

### Found (`§13`, `SEO.md`)

16. **`robots.txt`** allows what should be crawled, and there is no production
    `noindex`. Check the live output, not the template
17. **Sitemap** lists live canonical URLs only, and is referenced from `robots.txt`
18. **One hostname, one protocol, one trailing-slash rule.** `http` redirects, apex
    and `www` resolve deliberately, single hop
19. **Redirects.** Sample the map, and verify **all** of the top-20-by-traffic rows.
    301, single hop, correct target
20. **Meta.** Titles and descriptions unique, present, in length. One `h1` per page,
    heading order intact. Canonicals absolute and self-referential
21. **Structured data** validates and matches visible content

### Converts (`§18`, hard)

22. **The funnel, end to end.** Run by `funnel-verifier`, and it is the check this
    loop exists for. See below
23. **Unfurl.** Paste the URL into a real client and look at the preview. Tags being
    present is not the preview rendering
24. **Every link.** Click all of them. Zero 404s, zero dead anchors, outbound links go
    where they claim

### Concrete starting points

```bash
mkdir -p runs/<slug>/shots/live
for w in 360 768 1440; do
  chrome --headless --window-size=$w,1400 --screenshot=runs/<slug>/shots/live/$w.png "<live-url>"
done
npx @axe-core/cli "<live-url>"
npx lighthouse "<live-url>" --preset=desktop --output=json --output-path=runs/<slug>/lh-desktop.json --quiet
npx lighthouse "<live-url>" --output=json --output-path=runs/<slug>/lh-mobile.json --quiet
npx lychee --no-progress "<live-url>"
curl -sI "https://<domain>" | head -20
curl -s "https://<domain>/robots.txt"
```

## The funnel proof (`§18`, hard)

`funnel-verifier` runs all of it, live, per [`MEASURE.md`](../MEASURE.md) §4:

1. Load with consent **rejected**. Confirm no analytics request goes out (`§16`)
2. Accept. Confirm exactly one `page_view`
3. Click the primary CTA. Confirm one `cta_click` with the right location property
4. Focus the form. Confirm one `form_start`
5. **Submit a real, clearly labeled test lead**
6. Confirm the success state renders, and `form_submit` fires **once**
7. Confirm the lead arrives at every destination: CRM record, inbox, channel
8. Confirm the autoresponder sends, and check it did not land in spam
9. Confirm the conversion appears in the analytics property, not just the network tab
10. Repeat on mobile and in the second-most-used browser
11. Trigger a validation error deliberately; confirm `form_error` fires with a reason
12. Delete or label the test lead so sales does not call it

**Steps 7 and 8 cannot be completed from a browser.** The agent reports them as
partial and the conductor confirms the far end with the client. An agent watching a
success message is not evidence a lead arrived, and claiming otherwise is the exact
failure `§18` exists to prevent.

Booking flow instead of a form? Book a real slot, confirm it appears on the calendar,
confirm the confirmation email, then cancel it.

## Then look at the screenshots yourself

The conductor does this, not an agent. Open every shot in `shots/live/` and look.
Automated checks pass on pages that are visibly wrong: a hero cropped at 768, a nav
that wraps into two lines, a CTA below the fold on a laptop, a product screenshot too
small to read.

## Handle failures

Fix what is fixable now, re-verify, and record both states. Log the rest with what it
would take to fix. **Never report a fix you did not confirm**, and never paper over a
failure with a caveat. If check 7 found axe violations, that goes on the first page of
the report, not in a footnote.

Two failures stop everything and get fixed before the run continues:

- A production `noindex` or a `Disallow: /` — the site is invisible and nobody will
  notice for weeks
- A form that does not deliver — the site looks fine and every lead is falling on the
  floor

## The report

`runs/<slug>/REPORT.md` opens with the grade and its reason, then the failures, then
everything else.

| Grade | Means |
|---|---|
| **A** | Full pipeline. Claims substantiated, positioning derived from real market and customer evidence, design validated at both gates, funnel proven live, instrumented and measurable |
| **B** | Core intact, some validation skipped. Strategy or design review thinner than ideal. Everything hard still held |
| **C** | Substance skipped — no VOC, no competitor work, or no real copy pass. A good-looking site making the client's own claims in the client's own words |
| **D** | Multiple substance skips, or shipped without measurement. A redesign whose effect nobody will ever know. Say exactly that |

Read `SKIPS.md` and grade against it. A **D** stated plainly is more useful than an
**A** claimed falsely.

Then: the live URL, all 24 checks with results, the screenshots, the Lighthouse and
CWV numbers, the funnel proof with the two partial steps flagged, the redirect
verification, what was skipped and what it cost, the rollback command, every claim you
flagged that the client overruled (`COMPLIANCE.md §8`), the baseline for Loop 8, and
what would move the grade up.

## Schedule Loop 8

Before closing this loop, agree the date. Two weeks minimum for a directional read,
four to six for anything actionable, longer on a low-traffic B2B site. Put it in the
report. A launch with no scheduled read is a launch nobody learns from.

## Skip cost

Skipping verification means the first person to find the broken form is a customer, and
the first person to notice the `noindex` is whoever wonders why traffic went to zero.

Skipping the funnel proof is not available (`§18`).

# webcrab

Turns a business into a deployed site that has a job. Agency sites, company sites,
product marketing sites, and landing pages — positioned, designed, written,
instrumented, live, and measured after real traffic.

It is an agent operating system: markdown instructions a capable coding agent
executes. There is nothing to install and no program to run.

```text
 BOOTSTRAP ─► MARKET ─► DESIGN ─► COPY ─► BUILD ─► CAPTURE ─► DEPLOY ─► VERIFY ─► MEASURE
    caps      & MESSAGE  2a dir   pages   code to  forms,     their     live      real
              intake→    2b craft written  the     CRM, SEO,  target,   funnel    traffic,
              VOC→crawl                    design  consent    redirects proof     next move
                 │         │  │                                  │
              Gate A      B1  B2                              Gate C
```

## Why

The default company website is a template with a logo dropped in. Centered hero over
a gradient, three feature cards, a logo bar, a testimonial slider, and a contact form
nobody has tested since launch. It converts badly, says nothing a competitor could
not say, and nobody can prove whether it works, because nobody instrumented it.

This pipeline forces the opposite:

- The message comes from **the words customers actually use** — mined from reviews,
  support tickets, and sales calls, not from the founder's roadmap vocabulary.
- The look is derived from **a position defended against the three competitors it has
  to beat**, not from taste or a reference site.
- **Every claim traces to a source**, because a number on a company site is an
  advertising claim, and the client carries it after you leave.
- **The conversion path is proven live** — a real submission, watched arriving at the
  far end. A form that posts to nowhere is the most expensive bug this pipeline can
  ship.
- **What ranks does not break.** A redirect map covers every existing URL before
  anything is replaced.
- **The run does not end at launch.** Loop 8 comes back after traffic and reads the
  numbers against the goal set in Loop 1.

## The doctrine

| File | What it governs |
|---|---|
| [`PRINCIPLES.md`](./PRINCIPLES.md) | The binding rules. Six are hard and never skip |
| [`POSITIONING.md`](./POSITIONING.md) | Strategy: ICP, jobs to be done, category, the message hierarchy, the proof ladder |
| [`CONVERSION.md`](./CONVERSION.md) | The offer, the objection ladder, the path, the forms |
| [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md) | How many pages, how they route, and who edits them without you |
| [`SEO.md`](./SEO.md) | Getting found, and not destroying what already ranks |
| [`COMPLIANCE.md`](./COMPLIANCE.md) | Consent, claims substantiation, customer logos, accessibility law |
| [`MEASURE.md`](./MEASURE.md) | What to instrument, and what a win looks like |
| [`STYLES.md`](./STYLES.md) | What it looks like. 30 styles, and how to collide them |
| [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md) | How you render it. The technique arsenal |
| [`MODELS.md`](./MODELS.md) | Which model tier runs which step, and why intake is not the cheap part |
| [`SKIPPING.md`](./SKIPPING.md) | What every step costs to leave out |
| [`PIPELINE.md`](./PIPELINE.md) | The map |

## The six that never skip

Everything else is optional. These are integrity, legal exposure, and not destroying
something that was working:

- **Every claim traces to evidence.** A number on a company site is an advertising
  claim, not a design detail.
- **Don't break what ranks.** Every existing URL gets a 301 before anything replaces
  it.
- **Consent before tracking.** Nothing fires before the visitor has agreed.
- **Accessibility basics.** A form nobody can complete with a keyboard is a lead you
  never knew you lost.
- **The conversion path is proven end to end**, with a real submission someone
  watched arrive.
- **Deploy is reversible, and you push as them.** Snapshot first, their credentials
  throughout.

Plus Gate C: nothing becomes publicly visible under a company's domain before the
person accountable for it has seen it.

## Four shapes

Landing page, small marketing site, marketing site with a blog, marketing site with a
CMS. Decided at Gate A, because it decides the stack and — the part that gets
skipped — who can change the pricing page on a Tuesday when you are not available.
[`ARCHITECTURE.md`](./ARCHITECTURE.md) covers the shapes, the routing, and the
handover.

## Deploy targets

Nine, including the client's own server as a first-class option: GitHub Pages,
Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, VPS with nginx, VPS with Docker, cPanel, S3 with
CloudFront, and agency handoff. The target constrains the stack, never the reverse.

## Running it

See [`HOW_TO_RUN.md`](./HOW_TO_RUN.md). In short: point your agent at this repo, give
it the client, and have it work the loops in order, stopping at each gate.

## Lineage

Sibling of [portfolio.me](https://github.com/PIIIX-org/portfolio.me), which does this
for a person, and [systemcicy](https://github.com/PIIIX-org/systemcicy), which does it
for a working digital product rather than a site about one. Same shape, different
problem: a portfolio argues that someone is good, a company site has to cause an
action and be able to prove it did.

Built by [PIIIX](https://github.com/PIIIX-org).

# How to run it

## Claude Code

Install as a plugin, then:

```
/webcrab <company name or domain>
```

Or point at the skill directly: "read `skills/webcrab/SKILL.md` and run the pipeline
for \<client\>."

## Any other capable agent

Point it at this repo and say:

> Read `PRINCIPLES.md`, then `skills/webcrab/SKILL.md`. Execute the loops in `loops/`
> in order for \<client\>. Stop at every gate and wait for my decision.

There is no program to install. The pipeline is markdown; the agent is the runtime.

## Before you start, get these

The run goes much better if the client brings them. Ask on day zero:

| Thing | Why | If they can't |
|---|---|---|
| **The goal in numbers** | `§0`. Everything is accountable to it | Loop 1 derives one with them, and Loop 8 sets a baseline instead of beating one |
| **Analytics access** | The baseline, and where the leads currently come from | Record the gap; Loop 5 installs measurement from zero |
| **Search Console access** | The authoritative list of what ranks (`§13`) | Crawl instead, and accept that orphan pages will be missed |
| **Who can say yes** | One name (`§1`) | Gate A stalls in committee. Get the name |
| **Brand assets** | Logo files, type licenses, a brand book if one exists | Loop 1 audits what is on the current site and extends from there |
| **Customer material** | Reviews, support tickets, sales-call notes, churn reasons | VOC falls back to public review sites only, which is thinner |
| **Claims they want to make** | Every number, with where it came from (`§6`) | Anything unsourced gets cut or hedged, and they find out at Gate A rather than at launch |
| **Permissions** | Customer logo consents, testimonial approvals (`§25`) | Class instead of instance: "a national grocery chain" |
| **CRM / inbox destination** | Where leads go, and who reads them (`§18`) | Handoff mode for the capture layer, flagged in the report |
| **Deploy access** | Host, DNS, repository — on their accounts (`§23`) | Handoff mode for deploy |

Drop documents into `runs/<slug>/inbox/` before Loop 1.

## What it will ask you

**Loop 0** — nothing. It checks its own capabilities and makes a run folder.

**Loop 1** — the intake. One question at a time, open-ended. This is the part that
decides whether the output is a marketing site or a brochure with a gradient. Budget
real time for it. It will also want to talk to sales and support, not just the
founder, and it will ask where the site deploys and who edits it afterward.

**Gate A** — you approve the strategy: the goal in numbers, ICP, positioning, the
offer, the objections that rank, which pages exist, the site shape, and the redirect
map.

**Gate B1** — you pick the concept from rendered design images.

**Gate B2** — you approve the techniques, motion, performance budget, and the list of
third-party tags with a named owner for each.

**Gate C** — you see the finished site before it goes public and before DNS moves.
This gate is not skippable.

**Loop 8** — a few weeks after launch, it comes back with the numbers and the next
three things to change.

## Skipping

Say so. Any step except six is optional. The agent states the cost once, records it,
and moves on. See [`SKIPPING.md`](./SKIPPING.md).

In a hurry: ask for **express mode**. Building one page for a campaign: ask for
**landing-page mode**.

## What you get

A live site on the infrastructure you picked, its source in your own repository, a
tested path for your own team to change it, and `runs/<slug>/REPORT.md` with an honest
confidence grade, the funnel proof, the rollback command, and the redirect map.

Then, after real traffic, `MEASURE.md`'s Loop 8 read: what moved, what didn't, what
confounded it, and the next three things worth doing.

 | `animation-timeline` | Native scroll-driven animation | Scroll effects off the main thread with no library. Check support, then fall back to `ScrollTrigger` |
 | Container queries | Components responding to their own box | Real art direction per component rather than per viewport. The correct tool for a project card that lives in three contexts |
 | CSS anchor positioning | Elements tethered to other elements | Annotations, tooltips, and marginalia that hold their relationship without JS measurement |

+| OKLCH gradients | Perceptual color space interpolation | Gradients with no gray dead zone in the middle. Free by default in CSS Color 4, which interpolates in Oklab unless an endpoint uses legacy sRGB syntax — `hex`, `rgb()`, `hsl()`. Write at least one endpoint as `oklch()` or `color(srgb …)` or the browser silently falls back to muddy sRGB mixing |
 | Morphing SVG paths | Interpolation between path definitions | Logos that transform, section markers that become something else |
 | Houdini paint worklets | Custom paint in a background image | Procedural texture inside CSS layout. Support is narrow, so always with a static fallback |
 | Conic / repeating gradients | Gradient functions used as pattern | Texture and moire at zero cost. Halftones, guilloche, radial rhythm |
 | `text-wrap: balance` / `pretty` | Native line-break optimization | Headlines that break where a designer would break them. One declaration |
 
+### Information design
+
+Zero dependencies, same as the group above. This is not chart styling — it is which
+channel carries the value, decided before a single pixel renders.
+
+| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
+|---|---|---|
+| Position-first encoding | The value sits on a shared scale as a position, not as a length, angle, area, or color alone | Position judgments run 1.4–2.5× more accurate than length and 1.96× more accurate than angle, with 5.3–7.3× fewer catastrophic misreads (Cleveland & McGill). Any stat block, comparison table, or before/after figure |
+| Perceptually-uniform color scales | Sequential scales built lightness-dominant, dark reading as more. Diverging scales mark their break with both hue and lightness together. Qualitative scales hold saturation and lightness near-constant and vary hue alone | ColorBrewer's construction grammar. A scale built this way survives greyscale and holds together for colorblind readers by construction. Caps near 7–9 classes before further division reads as noise |
+| No rainbow, ever | Jet and rainbow-family colormaps stay off the table regardless of the palette elsewhere on the page | A bright mid-range band reads as a false peak — measured brighter than the true data maximum by a wide margin. The distortion hits every reader, not only colorblind ones |
+
 ### Motion and input
 
 Motion is where a portfolio proves the person can control time. Every entry here
@@ -112,7 +123,7 @@ is bound by `§12`: a designed reduced-motion state ships with it.
 | Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
 |---|---|---|
 | Scrubbed scroll timelines | Progress tied to scroll position | Scroll as a scrub head. The visitor controls the story instead of watching it |
-| View Transitions API | Native cross-document and same-document morphs | Continuity between pages. A project thumbnail that becomes the case study hero |
+| View Transitions API | Native cross-document and same-document morphs. Cross-document needs `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` on both pages, same-origin only, and browsers without support just ignore the unknown at-rule — safe with zero fallback code | Continuity between pages. A project thumbnail that becomes the case study hero, because the browser keeps the new state live rather than snapshotting it, so anything still running (a playing video) keeps running through the transition |
 | Custom cursors | The pointer replaced or augmented | Signals a designed environment within one second. Costs almost nothing |
 | Magnetic elements | Targets attracted to the pointer within a radius | Interactive surfaces that feel weighted. Best on a few elements only |
 | Spring and inertia physics | Motion resolved by simulation rather than easing | Motion that responds to how the input arrived. Nothing else feels this alive |
@@ -139,6 +150,7 @@ ceiling for everything else.
 | Sound design | Considered audio on interaction and ambience | Opt-in, never autoplay, always with a visible mute. When it fits, nobody else did it |
 | Procedural texture synthesis | Surface generated rather than downloaded | Grain, paper, fabric, and noise at zero request cost, tuned exactly to the palette |
 | Generated-then-treated imagery | Image tool output run through in-browser treatment | `§10`. Duotone, displacement, dithering, or grain applied in the browser. Raw output never reaches the page |
+| The absence states | The 404, the empty blog index, the failed contact submission — pages nobody plans to design | The single likeliest place a visitor meets the generic template underneath everything, because it is the page nobody thought to design. Built from the same collision and concept as the rest of the site, never a framework default |
 
 ### Typographic craft
 
@@ -199,6 +211,18 @@ That asymmetry is the reason this loop exists.
 A gradient hero, an SVG filter, a clip-path reveal, and a `@property` animation
 all sit in tier 1 and cost close to nothing.
 
+### Motion that doesn't cost layout shift
+
+LCP is not the only budget in this section — CLS is a Core Web Vital too, and it is
+failed by the animation choices this file spends the most time recommending.
+
+Compositor-thread properties — `transform` (translate, scale, rotate, skew) and
+`opacity` — never trigger a layout shift, by definition. Animating `top`, `left`,
+`width`, `height`, or `box-shadow` does, every time, on every frame. The fix is
+never "animate it more carefully"; it is animating a different property. A hover
+lift moves on `transform: translateY()`, never on `top`. A glow grows on a
+pseudo-element's `opacity`, never on `box-shadow` spread.
+
 ### Deferring a WebGL scene
 
 1. Ship a **static poster** in the shell. A gradient, an SVG, or a treated still

content.content:
96	| Edge detection / sobel | Gradient magnitude as outline | Blueprint and diagram registers. Pairs with posterize |
97	| Vignette | Falloff toward the frame | Directs the eye. Invisible when right, obvious when missing |
98	| Motion blur | Accumulated or velocity-buffer smear | Speed that reads as speed rather than strobe |
99	
100	### CSS and SVG native
101	
102	The cheapest wins in the file. Most of this costs nothing in bytes and nothing in
103	main-thread time, which makes it the right first reach on a site with a performance
104	budget (`§19`).
105	
106	| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
107	|---|---|---|
108	| OKLCH color and gradients | Perceptual color space | Gradients with no gray dead zone. Use it everywhere and the palette improves for free |
109	| `@property` | Typed, animatable custom properties | Gradients, angles, and colors that actually interpolate. CSS-only effects that used to need JS |
110	| `animation-timeline` | Native scroll-driven animation | Scroll effects off the main thread with no library. Check support, fall back to a library |
111	| View Transitions API | Native cross-document and same-document morphs | Continuity between pages. A pricing tier that becomes the signup form |
112	| Container queries | Components responding to their own box | Real art direction per component. Correct for a card living in three contexts |
113	| CSS anchor positioning | Elements tethered to other elements | Annotations, tooltips, and marginalia without JS measurement |
114	| SVG filters | `feTurbulence`, `feDisplacementMap`, `feColorMatrix` | Procedural noise, warping, and duotone on live DOM. Text and images, no canvas |
115	| The gooey filter | Blur into contrast matrix | Metaball merging on real HTML elements. Nav items that fuse |
116	| Masks and clip-paths | Alpha, luminance, and geometric clipping | Non-rectangular layout. The fastest exit from the card grid |
117	| `mix-blend-mode` | Compositing between stacked layers | Type that reacts to what passes behind it. Inverting cursors |
118	| `backdrop-filter` | Filtering what sits behind an element | Real depth in sticky UI and nav |
119	| Conic / repeating gradients | Gradient functions as pattern | Texture and moiré at zero byte cost |
120	| Morphing SVG paths | Interpolation between path definitions | A logo that transforms into the product's core shape |
121	| `text-wrap: balance` / `pretty` | Native line-break optimization | Headlines that break where a designer would. One declaration |
122	| `:has()` | Parent and sibling selection | State-driven layout with no JS. Form states, filled-field styling, section adaptation |
123	| Houdini paint worklets | Custom paint in a background image | Procedural texture inside CSS layout. Narrow support, always with a fallback |
124	
125	### Motion and input
126	
127	| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
128	|---|---|---|
129	| Scrubbed scroll timelines | Progress tied to scroll position | Scroll as a scrub head. Use for one section, never a whole marketing page |
130	| Spring and inertia physics | Motion resolved by simulation | Interfaces that respond to how the input arrived |
131	| Magnetic elements | Targets attracted to the pointer | Weighted feel on the primary CTA. A few elements only |
132	| Custom cursors | The pointer replaced or augmented | Signals a designed environment within a second. Desktop only — design mobile first |
133	| Variable fonts on all axes | Scroll or pointer driving every axis | Optical size, width, grade, slant. **Weight alone is the amateur signal** — read the font's axis list |
134	| Per-glyph transforms | Individual characters in 3D | Headlines that assemble and settle. High effort, high recall |
135	| Split-text stagger | Sequencing at glyph or word level | Entrances with rhythm. The enabler for most of this group |
136	| Scroll-velocity distortion | Scroll speed feeding a shader or filter | The site responds to how fast someone moves. Subtle, immediately felt |
137	| Cursor-as-light-source | Pointer driving a mask or light position | Reveals and spotlights the visitor navigates by hand |
138	| Pointer-tilt / device orientation | Gyroscope driving parallax | Depth on mobile where there is no hover. Permission-aware fallback |
139	| Number roll-ups on reveal | Counting to a real figure | Only for rank-1 numbers, and only once per page. Otherwise it is a tic |
140	
141	### Whole-page moves
142	
143	| Technique | What it is | Where it earns its place |
144	|---|---|---|
145	| Designed preloader | A composed hold, not a spinner | Only when there is genuinely something to wait for. Never in front of a static page |
146	| Cross-document View Transitions | Page-to-page continuity | A multi-page site that feels like one surface, with no framework |
147	| Progressive disclosure | Depth revealed on demand | The committee problem: a skimmable page that a deep reader can open up |
148	| Sticky section pinning | A section held while its content advances | One per page, maximum. Two is a tunnel |
149	| Scroll-linked nav state | Nav adapting to position and direction | Keeps the CTA reachable without a permanent bar eating the viewport |
150	| Print stylesheet | A real one | Procurement prints pricing pages. It costs 30 lines and someone will thank you |
151	| Reduced-data mode | `prefers-reduced-data` respected | Drop the heavy layer entirely. Cheap, and honest |
152	
153	---
154	
155	## The cheap wins
156	
157	If a run only has budget for a handful of moves, these are the ones with the best
158	return per byte on a commercial site:
159	
160	1. **Real product UI, well shot and annotated** (`§11`)
161	2. **A visible price** — a design decision as much as a business one
162	3. **OKLCH palette with a properly built neutral ramp** — makes everything else better
163	4. **A real type system with one variable font on more than one axis**
164	5. **`text-wrap: balance` on every headline** — one line, immediate
165	6. **A 12-second real screen recording, poster-first**
166	7. **Named, faced, sourced proof placed next to the claim it supports**
167	8. **A form that is three fields and works** (`§18`)
168	9. **Print stylesheet and a proper OG image** — both invisible until someone needs them
169	10. **One collision-carrying signature moment**, prototyped, that no competitor has
170	
171	## Prototyping
172	
173	Loop 2b, one agent per technique, in `runs/<slug>/prototypes/`.
174	
175	Free rein while prototyping: any library, any CDN, any reference. That freedom ends
176	at Loop 4, where everything gets downloaded, vendored, and committed (`§14`).
177	
178	Each prototype delivers: a standalone runnable HTML file, a screenshot, a measured
179	frame rate under load on throttled hardware, the byte cost, and all three states.
180	Then a verdict — ship, cut, or ship-with-caveat. **Report failure honestly**; failing
181	cheap here is the entire point of the loop.
182	
183	## Performance discipline
184	
185	`§19`, restated as build rules:
186	
187	- Shell under 100KB. It paints something real with no JS at all
188	- Heavy layer lazy-loaded after first paint, gated on intersection, never in the LCP
189	  path. It declares its number at Gate B2
190	- Hero image preloaded, correctly sized, modern format, explicit dimensions
191	- Fonts self-hosted, subset, `font-display: swap`, and preloaded if they are in the
192	  LCP element
193	- Every third-party tag deferred and consented (`§15`, `§16`)
194	- No layout shift after paint. Reserve space for everything that arrives late,
195	  including the cookie banner
196	- Measure on a throttled mid-range Android, not on the machine you built it on
197	
198	A technique that cannot be deferred has to justify its bytes at Gate B2, in front of
199	the client, against the conversion goal.
200	
201	## The three states, always
202	
203	Every technique, every time (`§17`):
204	
205	| State | What it is |
206	|---|---|
207	| **Full** | The designed experience |
208	| **Reduced motion** | An **art-directed still** — a composed frame someone designed. Never `animation: none` |
209	| **Fallback** | No WebGL, no JS, old GPU, blocked script. A real page, never an apology |
210	
211	The fallback is not a degraded mode; it is a design deliverable. On a company site it
212	is also a commercial one, because the visitor on locked-down corporate hardware with
213	scripts restricted is frequently the enterprise buyer.

### Motion that does not cost layout shift

LCP is not the only budget here. CLS is a Core Web Vital too, and it is failed by the
animation choices this file spends the most time recommending.

Compositor-thread properties — `transform` (translate, scale, rotate, skew) and
`opacity` — never trigger a layout shift, by definition. Animating `top`, `left`,
`width`, `height`, or `box-shadow` does, every time, on every frame. The fix is never
"animate it more carefully"; it is animating a different property. A hover lift moves
on `transform: translateY()`, never on `top`. A glow grows on a pseudo-element's
`opacity`, never on `box-shadow` spread.

## Style and accessibility

`§17` is hard. Each of these fails a specific criterion by default; each has a fix
that keeps the style.

| Style | What it fights | The fix that ships |
|---|---|---|
| **Glass / refractive** | Text contrast changes with whatever scrolls behind it | An opaque or near-opaque scrim behind every text run, measured against the *worst* frame of the moving substrate, never a still |
| **Cinematic dark / nocturne** | Vignette, grade, and grain push small type below threshold | Measure contrast on the rendered pixels after grade and grain. Body copy stays out of the falloff. Grain opacity drops on text layers |
| **Letterpress / debossed** | Form is shadow on one hue, so nothing has a ratio | Extrusion for containers only. Every label and control state gets a real foreground token at ≥4.5:1. Focus is a hard visible ring, never a deeper shadow |
| **Kinetic / physics / scroll-cinema** | Motion is the design, so removing motion removes the site | An art-directed still: a composed frame with type at rest that someone designed. Scroll-cinema degrades to a paginated document, same content, same order |
| **Spatial / 3D** | Navigation depends on a camera and a GPU | Keyboard traversal between named places, a text route to every section, and a no-WebGL fallback that is a real page rather than an apology |
| **Terminal** | Scanlines and curvature reduce legibility and can trigger | Curvature and scanline opacity behind `prefers-reduced-motion`, plus a visible toggle. Body text on the flat layer above the effect |
| **Comparison / data-dense** | Density defeats zoom and reflow | Real table semantics with scoped headers, keyboard-reachable scroll containers, a stated minimum readable width, and a genuine mobile layout rather than a shrunken desktop one |
| **Neo-brutalist** | Clashing color chosen for energy rather than ratio | Pick the clash in OKLCH and check every pair. Loud and 4.5:1 are compatible; loud and untested is not |
| **Aurora / gradient fields** | Text over a moving gradient has no fixed ratio | Freeze the gradient behind text, or scrim it. Measure against the worst frame |
| **Typographic-led** | Enormous display type reflowing at 320px | A real mobile type scale, not a scaled-down desktop one. Test at 320px and at 200% zoom |

## Light and dark as two designs

# Loop 3 — Copy

**Goal:** every string that will appear on the site, written in the customer's words,
mapped to the message hierarchy, with every factual claim checked against
`EVIDENCE.md`.

**Input:** `BRIEF.md` (message hierarchy, objection ladder, VOC extract, voice),
`EVIDENCE.md`, `DIRECTION.md` (so the copy fits the design that exists).

**Output:** `COPY.md`.

---

## Why this comes before Build

Design built around placeholder text breaks when real text arrives. A hero designed
for six words gets a fourteen-word headline, a feature card designed for two lines
gets five, and the fix is either worse copy or a redesign — and under deadline it is
always worse copy.

On a marketing site this matters more than anywhere else, because **the copy is the
product.** A visitor does not experience the layout; they read a sentence and decide.
Design serves that sentence.

## The rule that governs this loop

`§5`: **write in the customer's words, not the company's.** The VOC extract in
`BRIEF.md` is not decoration. Open it, and use those phrases for problems, symptoms,
and outcomes. The company register from `POSITIONING.md §11` governs tone; the
customer lexicon governs nouns and verbs.

The single most common failure: a hero line describing what the software *is*, in the
vocabulary of the roadmap, to a visitor who came looking for a solution to a symptom.

## The headline

Top-tier work, and the conductor writes it rather than a worker. It is one line
carrying the positioning, the customer's language, and the top objection at once, and
it is the highest-leverage sentence on the site.

Write at least eight. Then test each against four checks:

| Check | Fails when |
|---|---|
| **Substitution** | A named competitor could put their name on it and it stays true |
| **Category** | A visitor cannot tell what kind of thing this is |
| **Language** | The main noun or verb came from the roadmap, not the VOC file |
| **Forwarding** | The champion cannot paste it into Slack and have it make sense alone |

Bring three survivors to the client, not one. And note: the best headline is often a
customer's sentence with two words removed.

## Page by page

Dispatch `page-writer`, one agent per page, in parallel. Each writes to the message
hierarchy and to the approved design image, and each checks every claim against
`EVIDENCE.md`.

Every page states, at the top of its section in `COPY.md`:

- **The one job** — the single action it exists to cause (`§7`)
- **Who lands here**, and from where
- **Which hierarchy levels it carries**
- **Which objections it answers**, in order

### The home page

Routes rather than explains. Its job is to make the right visitor go one level deeper,
not to say everything. The most common failure is a home page trying to be the product
page, the about page, and the pricing page at once.

Structure follows the objection ladder, not convention. If the top objection is trust,
proof comes before features. If it is fit, the vertical evidence comes before
anything.

### Product and service pages

One per genuinely distinct offering. Lead with the outcome in the customer's words,
then the mechanism, then the proof. Features are the third thing on the page, never
the first — a feature list answers "what is it" for someone who has already decided
they want it.

Show the product (`§11`). The copy's job is to frame the screenshot, not to substitute
for it.

### Pricing

Per `CONVERSION.md §5`. Tiers named for who they are for. The recommended one
obviously recommended, with an honest reason. Every inclusion claim checked (`§6`) —
"unlimited" had better be unlimited. An FAQ under the table answering overages, seats,
notice period, and what happens to the data if they leave.

### Case studies

Five beats, and the fourth is the one everyone cuts:

**Problem** — what was wrong before, in the customer's words
**Constraint** — what made it hard, and why the obvious fix did not work
**Decision** — the call, and what it gave up
**What broke** — the thing that went wrong. Keep this beat
**Outcome** — sourced, dated, ranked (`§6`)

Named customer, named person, real numbers, cleared (`§25`). The customer's own words
wherever you have them. A case study with no friction in it reads as marketing,
because it is.

Under NDA: write the class of problem instead of the instance. "A payments platform
processing nine figures a year" carries the weight; the logo does not. Anonymized
still has to be true, and it traces to `EVIDENCE.md` exactly as a named claim does.

### Comparison pages

The highest-value page most sites do not have, and the highest-risk one
(`COMPLIANCE.md §2`). Every claim about the competitor sourced, dated, and linked to
their own material. Compare on dimensions a buyer weighs. **Say where they are
genuinely better** — a table where one column wins every row is read as marketing
rather than information, and it converts worse for exactly that reason.

### About

Answers the trust objection, and on an agency site it is frequently the second most
visited page. Real people with real names and real photographs (`§25` — never
generated). What the company is for, what it refuses, who is accountable. Not a
founding-myth paragraph about a problem the founders noticed.

### The small print

Nav labels, buttons, form labels and help text, validation errors in plain words,
empty states, the success state, the autoresponder email, the 404 page, the footer,
and the legal pages' plain-language summaries. This is where sites reveal whether
anyone was paying attention.

Error messages are copy. "Something went wrong" is an unwritten string.

## Objections, placed

`§9`: place the answer where the objection occurs, not collected in a bottom FAQ.

Walk the objection ladder from `BRIEF.md` and assign each one a location in a specific
page at a specific point. The `COPY.md` template has a table for it. An objection with
no location assigned has not been answered — it has been listed.

An FAQ section is still useful for the long tail and for search. It is not where the
top three objections live.

## Calls to action

Per `CONVERSION.md §3`. Say what happens, not what to do. State the cost next to the
ask. One primary per page. Never "Submit".

Write the microcopy under the button too — "No card. Two minutes." removes the
objection at the exact point of decision, and it is three words.

## The prose pass

Three passes, in order, on everything:

1. **`stop-slop`** — strip the AI tells: the "not X, but Y" contrast, the em-dash tic,
   the reflexive three-item list, the hollow superlative (`§20`)
2. **`copywriting`** — clarity, specificity, rhythm, the promise in the first line
3. **`ogilvy`** — does it sell, and would the reader act

Then read it aloud. Anything you stumble on is a sentence a visitor will skim.

Note in `COPY.md` anything the passes changed materially — it is a useful signal about
whether the source material was thin.

## The evidence check

Before `COPY.md` is done, cross-reference every factual statement against
`EVIDENCE.md` (`§6`, hard):

- Every number has a source and a date
- Every superlative has substantiation, or it is cut
- Every comparison links to the competitor's own material
- Every testimonial has an approval on file
- Every logo has a written permission (`§25`)
- Every certification claim matches an actual certificate — "in progress" is never
  "compliant"

Anything failing goes back to the client as a question, not out as a silent cut. They
frequently have the source and did not know you needed it.

## Reading level and length

Write for the person who will forward this, on a phone, between meetings. Short
sentences. The claim first, the qualification second. No paragraph over four lines on
mobile.

Length follows the decision, not a rule: a £40k contract needs more page than a £19
subscription, and both need every line to earn its place. Cut anything that does not
map to a hierarchy level.

## Localization

If the site ships in more than one language (`§26`), copy is written per locale, not
translated at the end. A translated hero with an English CTA is worse than an English
site. Number and date formats, name order, and address shapes are copy decisions too.

## Skip cost

Skipping copy means the design gets built around placeholder lengths and then breaks,
and the client writes the words at the last minute in their own vocabulary — which
undoes `§5` and most of Loop 1 with it.

Skipping the objection mapping means the answers collect in a bottom FAQ, where
objections go to be ignored.

Skipping the evidence check is not available (`§6`).

# Loop 4 — Build

**Goal:** the site exists, coded to the approved images, with real copy in it, in all
three states, under budget, and editable by the client.

**Input:** `DIRECTION.md`, the design images, `COPY.md`, the prototypes.

**Output:** the site, in the client's repository.

---

## Stack

Settled at Gate A (`ARCHITECTURE.md`). Default is hand-authored HTML and CSS with
committed assets — it runs on all nine deploy targets and it is the fastest thing that
can be built. A publishing cadence moves it to a generator; a non-technical editor
moves it to a CMS.

**Do not ship a framework to the browser for a marketing site.** It is the most common
reason a company site fails Core Web Vitals, and Core Web Vitals are a ranking input
(`§19`). A generator that outputs static HTML is a build-time tool and is fine.

## The shell contract, first

Before any page is built, one person builds the shell and everything else consumes it.
Parallel page builds that each invent their own spacing scale produce a site that
looks assembled, which is exactly what this pipeline exists to avoid.

The shell owns:

### The token file

One file. Every value in it, nothing hardcoded anywhere else.

- Color: substrate, surfaces, text ramp, accent, and the full state set — error,
  success, warning, focus, disabled. Both modes, art-directed separately
- Type: families, the scale, line heights, measures, and the separate mobile scale
- Space: one scale, used everywhere
- Radius, border, shadow: the small set the design actually uses
- Motion: durations and easings from the motion spec, and the reduced-motion values
- Breakpoints and container widths
- Z-index: a named ladder, so the sticky CTA and the cookie banner and the nav do not
  fight in production

### The head

Charset, viewport, title and description per page, canonical, OG and Twitter tags,
favicon set, theme-color, preloads for the LCP image and any font in the LCP element,
and the JSON-LD block. Loop 5 fills the per-page values; the shape lives here.

### The frame

Skip link, header, nav, footer, and the `§27` attribution. Keyboard reachable, current
page indicated, works at 360px, and present on every page including the deepest post.

### The primitives

Buttons, links, form fields, labels, help text, error and success states, tables,
cards, and the section wrapper. Every one with hover, focus-visible, active, and
disabled states designed rather than defaulted.

Build the form primitives properly here, once. They are the `§18` surface and every
page reuses them.

## Fan out

Dispatch `page-builder`, one agent per page, each in its own git worktree so parallel
builds do not collide. Each agent codes **its page only** — never the shell, never the
tokens, never another page's section.

Give each one: its design image, its copy from `COPY.md`, the shell contract, the
technique assignment from `DIRECTION.md`, and the prototype for that technique.

When an agent finds a spec ambiguity, it reports rather than deciding. A builder
inventing a spacing value is how a design system quietly gets a second one.

## Code to the image

The approved design image is the spec. Match the composition, the type scale, the
spacing rhythm, the crop, and the color. Where the image and the copy disagree —
because real copy is longer than the render assumed — the copy wins and the layout
adapts. Note it, so the pattern shows up if it repeats.

Do not redesign during the build. If the image is wrong, that goes back to the
conductor, not into the code.

## Responsive

Three widths minimum, real designs at each: 360, 768, 1440. Not one design that
shrinks.

- **Mobile first, actually.** Most B2B traffic is now mobile, including the buying
  committee's first look, and the champion frequently forwards a link that gets opened
  on a phone
- Fluid type with clamps, and a separate mobile type scale where the display sizes
  need one
- Container queries for components living in more than one context
- Test at 320px and at 200% zoom — both are `§17` requirements and both break
  display-scale typography
- Tables get a real mobile design, not a horizontal scroll of the desktop table
- The primary CTA is reachable on mobile without hunting. A sticky ask is allowed if
  it does not cover the content that argues for it

## Images and media

- Modern formats with fallbacks, `srcset` and `sizes` real rather than decorative
- Explicit `width` and `height` on everything, always. Layout shift after paint is a
  Core Web Vitals failure and the cheapest one to avoid
- LCP image preloaded, correctly sized, never lazy-loaded
- Everything below the fold lazy
- Descriptive `alt` on every image (`§17`), meaningful filenames (`SEO.md`)
- Video: poster image in the shell, player loaded on interaction, never autoplay with
  sound, captions on anything with speech
- Product screenshots at the resolution that makes the UI legible — a blurred
  dashboard is worse than no dashboard (`§11`)

## The three states, per section

Every technique, every time (`§17`):

| State | What ships |
|---|---|
| **Full** | The designed experience |
| **Reduced motion** | An art-directed still. A composed frame someone designed, never `animation: none` |
| **Fallback** | No WebGL, no JS, blocked scripts, old GPU. A real page, never an apology |

The fallback matters commercially here: the visitor on locked-down corporate hardware
is frequently the enterprise buyer.

## Forms

Built here, wired in Loop 5. Per `CONVERSION.md §4`:

- Semantic markup, visible associated labels, correct `type` and `autocomplete`
- Validate on blur, errors next to the field in words, announced to assistive tech
- **Never clear the form on error.** Never lose what they typed
- Submit disabled only while in flight, with a changed label
- Real success state on the page, saying what happens next and when
- Failure state with a route out — an email address to write to instead
- Honeypot and a time-to-submit threshold (`CONVERSION.md §4`)
- It works with JavaScript disabled, or it degrades to a `mailto:` that at least tells
  the visitor the truth

## Vendor everything (`§14`)

Before the build is done: every library, font, and icon downloaded, committed, and
served from the client's own origin. No CDN in production. Pin versions. Keep the
licenses in the repo (`COMPLIANCE.md §3`).

Prototypes were allowed to pull from anywhere. That freedom ends here.

## Third-party tags

Only the ones approved at Gate B2, each loaded after consent (`§16`) and after first
paint (`§15`). None of them in the LCP path. Reserve space for anything that injects
into the layout, including the cookie banner — a banner that shifts the page after
paint is a CLS failure the compliance team mandated and nobody measured.

## Editability

Whatever was decided at Gate A (`ARCHITECTURE.md`), build it now rather than
retrofitting:

- Content collections with typed frontmatter, if a generator
- CMS schema with typed fields — heading, body, image with **required** alt text — and
  no way to set a color or a font size
- Preview before publish, drafts that do not leak into RSS or the sitemap
- A build that cannot deploy a broken page

A rich-text blob on a designed page is how a careful design system becomes eleven font
sizes in a month.

## Quality passes

Start with the mechanical half, which is one command:

```bash
python3 scripts/preflight.py runs/<slug>/site --evidence runs/<slug>/EVIDENCE.md
```

It catches the silent ones — a stray `noindex`, a CDN asset nobody vendored, a form
with no action, an unlabelled field, a figure that is not in `EVIDENCE.md`. It does not
judge design, prose, or whether a claim is true, and passing it discharges no hard
rule. Fix what it finds, then run the rest by hand:

| Pass | Check |
|---|---|
| **Semantics** | One `h1` per page, heading order unskipped, landmarks, lists that are lists |
| **Keyboard** | Tab the whole site. Visible focus, no traps, skip link works, modals return focus |
| **axe** | Zero violations, not zero criticals |
| **Contrast** | Measured on the rendered pixels, including over imagery and translucency |
| **Copy** | Every string from `COPY.md`, none invented during the build, no lorem left |
| **Claims** | Nothing on the page that is not in `EVIDENCE.md` (`§6`) |
| **Budget** | Shell under 100KB, heavy layer deferred, third-party within its number |
| **Console** | Zero errors on load and after a full scroll |
| **Links** | Every internal link resolves. No dead anchors |
| **Print** | The pricing page prints. Procurement prints pricing pages |
| **No-JS** | The page renders and the content is readable |

## Local screenshots

Screenshot every template at 360, 768, and 1440, in both color modes and with reduced
motion forced, into `runs/<slug>/shots/local/`. Look at them yourself. This is a
rehearsal for Loop 7, and it is much cheaper to fix here.

## Attribution (`§27`)

Small footer credit, "Built with webcrab", linking to the repo and to PIIIX, plus the
marker comment. Visible, never hidden. Tell the client it is there and that removing
it is fine.

## Skip cost

Skipping the quality passes moves cross-browser and responsive failures from before
deploy to after it, where the client finds them.

Skipping the vendoring step leaves the site depending on public endpoints that will
eventually go down and leave it broken, on a domain the client's customers visit.

Skipping editability means retrofitting a CMS onto a hand-authored site later, which
is a rebuild of the templates.

Ported and pushed to PR #1: https://github.com/PIIIX-org/webcrab/pull/1

The changes were real — your local portfolio.me clone was 4 commits behind. PRs #2 and #3 (merged yesterday and this morning) touched five files; I hit the same five in webcrab. Adapted, not transplanted — webcrab's a parallel rewrite, so portfolio's `§12` is this repo's `§17`, "projects" become tiers and case studies, and so on.

What came over:

- **OKLCH was wrong by omission** — CSS Color 4 interpolates in Oklab for free, but one `hex`/`rgb()` endpoint silently drops it back to sRGB. Loop 2a repeated the same incomplete advice; both fixed.
- **Information design table** — position-first encoding, ColorBrewer scale construction, no rainbow. This lands harder on a company site than a portfolio: stat blocks, pricing comparisons, ROI figures are all proof points under `§10`, and the false-peak problem usually sits in the chart arguing for the product.
- **View Transitions** — the `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` requirement, same-origin, no fallback needed.
- **Absence states** — CRAFT entry plus a Loop 2a concept bullet, a Loop 3 note, a Loop 4 quality pass. After a migration the 404 is high-traffic, and the failed-submission state is read by someone mid-conversion.
- **CLS section** — transform/opacity vs top/left/width/height/box-shadow. CRAFT spends most of its length recommending exactly the animations that fail the Core Web Vital `§19` makes a budget.

Two I adapted rather than copied: the neo-brutalism row got **merged** into webcrab's existing one (border-weight hierarchy is a different failure from an untested contrast pair — two rows would have been redundant), and the card-grid critique went into "how proof is presented", where it bites hardest on comparable things like tiers and competitors.

Didn't port portfolio.me PR #1 — it was closed unmerged.

Kept it on the same branch as a second commit rather than opening a stacked PR, since both touch `loops/04-build.md`.

The account thing bit again mid-session: `gh` had flipped back to sadeqisaidmohaddes-star on its own and the push 403'd. Re-switched and it went through. Worth pinning down why it keeps reverting before the next PIIIX-org push.
